artworks.description: The image features two sketched illustrations on two separate pages. On the left page is an illustration of a woman sitting down, holding an orange. She is dressed in a long-sleeved outfit with rolled-up sleeves and an apron, and has medium-length wavy hair. She is surrounded by a basket of oranges. The background is textured. On the right page is an illustration of a woman standing on a beam over water, with her upper body extended forward and arms outstretched. She has short curly hair and wears a skirt. Several figures in the background are observing her, with indistinct architectural elements around them.

artworks.title: André Antoine
artworks.medium: photomechanical process on wove paper
artworks.description: The image features a drawing of a man's head and upper chest facing forward. The man has prominent eyes, a straight nose, and a small mustache above his upper lip. His hair is short and combed to the side. He appears to be wearing a collared shirt. The background is plain, and the name "ANDRÉ ANTOINE" is written below the drawing.

artworks.title: Inceste d'âmes; Mineur et soldat
artworks.medium: 4-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: The image features a landscape with a horizontal line where the sun sets or rises against an orange and brown terrain. The horizon is in the upper third of the image, the sun partially visible, casting a golden hue. Two figures are standing near two tall trees on the right side. The painting style is reminiscent of lithographic prints, with a dreamlike quality in the brushstrokes. The color palette includes blues and earth tones, with the sun in bright yellow. Another figure is on the ground to the right. The colors subtly shift from warm to cool, creating a serene composition.

artworks.title: Inceste d'âmes; Mineur et soldat
artworks.medium: 5-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a painting of a theatrical poster showing a scenic landscape with two figures under a tree, one pointing towards the horizon where the sun sets over a mountain range. Another figure sits to the right. The foreground displays text detailing a theater production.

artworks.description: This is a drawing of a theater program cover. The title "Le Théâtre Libre" is displayed in an ornate, flowing script curving across the page. The words "Saison 1888-89" are near the top in a bolder style, while additional text lists a location "Au Théâtre des Menus-Plaisirs, 14 Boulevard de Strasbourg." Below the title is an illustration of a man's profile within a circular frame with the initials "JFR." The drawing is done with black ink on beige paper.

artworks.title: La Cloche engloutie
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a stylized advertisement or program cover for a theatrical performance. The left half of the image features an intricately drawn figure with long hair seated near an anthropomorphic creature or caricature with a rounded face, all within a lush, patterned setting. The design includes ornate text with detailing, mentioning "L'Œuvre" and "La Cloche Engloutie." The composition combines fantasy and Art Nouveau influences with flowing lines and decorative motifs.

artworks.title: Le Repas du lion
artworks.medium: photolithograph in red on wove paper
artworks.description: The image shows a sketch by Auguste Rodin on the right side of a theatre program from Théâtre Antoine. The drawing depicts a full-body view of a person in a seated position with one hand resting on their chin and the other arm draped across their knee. The person's head is tilted slightly forward, and while facial features lack detail, the outline suggests contemplation. The figure appears to be enveloped in loose, flowing attire. There is no visible jewelry or objects held by the figure. The background of the sketch section is a uniform beige tone, contrasting with the detailed calligraphy and printed text on the left side of the program. The text provides details about the play "Le Repas du Lion," including the title, playwright, and cast list for the performance dated to the 1897-1898 season.

artworks.title: L'Ecole de l'idéal; Le Petit Eyolf
artworks.medium: photomechanical process on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a theatrical program. The document displays a printed theater program for performances of "L'école de l'idéal" by Paul Véron and "Le petit Eyolf" by Henrik Ibsen, scheduled on the 8th and 9th of May, 1895. The program details the cast for each play and the roles they perform, with the left side displaying an illustrated sketch of two figures in a dynamic pose against a textured background. The illustration is signed by Felicien Rops on the right side of the page.

artworks.title: L'Ecole de l'idéal; Le Petit Eyolf
artworks.medium: photomechanical process on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a theatre program featuring a sketch of a classical figure. The image shows a printed programme for performances on the 8th and 9th of May, 1895, at L'Œuvre, a theatre offering two plays: "L'École de l'Idéal" by Paul Vérôla and "Le Petit Eyolf" by Henrik Ibsen, translated by Comte Prozor. The top of the program includes a drawing by Félicien Rops, depicted as an outline sketch of a nude, helmeted figure holding a cloth-wrapped head. The drawing is minimalistic with fine line work. The program text is arranged around the drawing, listing play titles, authors, and actors, with neatly organized columns and dots suggesting cast names. The paper is an aged, brownish color.

artworks.title: Hérakléa
artworks.medium: zincograph in red-brown on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: The image captures a detailed landscape from an elevated perspective. A body of water with distant ships is seen, alongside soldiers or figures on horseback labeled "P. Ser." The terrain is rugged with figures engaged in various activities. The style features bold lines suggestive of woodcut or linocut techniques, using a monochromatic sepia color palette. Romanesque-style buildings are present on the left side of the image.

artworks.title: L'Assomption de Hannele Mattern; En l'attendant
artworks.medium: 5-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a painting of a theatrical poster. The central portion of the image shows a scene involving a reclining figure with elongated limbs, another figure seemingly floating above, and a stylized large face in the background. The painting is in the style of Alphonse Mucha and features soft, muted colors typical of Art Nouveau, with a predominant use of browns and greens. The figures are outlined with fluid lines. Surrounding the visual scene, text is featured prominently, providing details about a play titled "L'Assomption de Hannele Mattern". The text, set in an elegant typeface, lists character names, performers, and production credits, situating the painting as a promotional piece for a theatrical performance.

artworks.title: L'Assomption de Hannele Mattern; En l'attendant
artworks.medium: 5-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a theater program cover. The image features a woman lying down on her back, holding a flower with a yellow center. The woman is drawn with a flowing sense of elegance, her hair cascading around her. In the background, there is a faint outline of another figure that blends into the overall green backdrop. The right side of the image contains text detailing a theater production, "L’Assomption de Hannele Mattern," listing the cast of characters and people involved in the performance. The style combines illustrative and typographic elements likely from the late 19th to early 20th century, creating an evocative and dreamy atmosphere.

artworks.title: Application du Cercle Chromatique de Mr. Ch. Henry
artworks.medium: color lithograph on card
artworks.description: The image consists of bold geometric shapes and lines creating an abstract composition. Large letters "T" and "L" are on the left and right, filled with colorful mosaic patterns. In the center, there is a black circle containing a vibrant pointillism-style scene of a sailboat on a seascape. Above and below the circle are colored strips featuring geometric patterns. The overall layout includes frame-like borders filled with checkerboard patterns.

artworks.title: Application du Cercle Chromatique de Mr. Ch. Henry
artworks.medium: color lithograph on card
artworks.description: The image displays bold geometric shapes, including a large circle intersected by a T and L shape. These shapes are filled with a mosaic of colors, giving the impression of stacked colored blocks. Inside the circle, there is an abstract representation of a person in headwear facing a sunset, depicted in a pixelated or pointillist style. The border of the image consists of lines and rectangles in contrasting colors, framing the central composition. The overall arrangement resembles a stained-glass window or a kaleidoscope art piece.

artworks.title: Application du Cercle Chromatique de Mr. Ch. Henry
artworks.medium: color lithograph on card
artworks.description: The image consists of geometric shapes and lines, including a large circle in the center and the bold letters "T" and "L" on either side. It features vibrant colors in a pointillism technique, with various shapes inside the letters and borders.

artworks.title: L'Ennemi du peuple
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a public event or theatrical performance. The drawing showcases a scene with a large, animated crowd facing a distinguished figure standing to the right side under the heading "L'ENNEEMI DU PEUPLE." The crowd appears lively with various expressions, some arms raised, and a few individuals in hats at the foreground. To the right, a list with names and roles accompanies the main figure, with the date "LE 18 FEVRIER 1899" included. The composition uses strong contrasts of light and shadow to convey energy and drama.

artworks.description: This is a drawing of two surreal compositions featuring symbolic elements related to French art and theatre. The left side of the image showcases an ethereal figure draped in cloth, blowing a horn labeled "Courrier Français," with a dark, menacing figure beside it. The right side of the image displays a shadowy figure moving dynamically amongst grave markers and thorny plants with a theatrical tone, accompanied by the text "Théâtre Libre" and "Décembre 1890." Both halves employ sepia tones and intricate line work.

artworks.title: Menu du réveillon offert aux amis du Théâtre Antoine
artworks.medium: lithograph in brown on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a menu accompanied by a sketch of a robed figure and a pig. The image features a handwritten menu titled "Menu du Réveillon" offered at "Théâtre Antoine," listing various dishes such as oysters, foie gras, salad, cheese, fruits, dessert, coffee, liqueurs, and champagne. On the right side of the image, there is a sketch of a figure dressed in robes, who appears to be communicating with a pig shown below them. The words "L'esprit de Sacrifice" are inscribed above, and below the pig, there's a note signed "Saint Antoine."

artworks.title: Menu du réveillon offert aux amis du Théâtre Antoine
artworks.medium: lithograph in brown on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a person wearing robes and a pig seated on the floor, with a handwritten menu. The drawing features a robed figure on the right, facing a pig on the left side of the image. The person is depicted in a loose, flowing robe looking downward toward the pig. The pig is drawn with its back to the viewer. In the middle of the image is a handwritten menu titled "MENU DU RÉVEILLON offert aux amis du Théatre Antoine," offering various dishes and beverages. The image contains an inscription at the top right reading "L'ESPRIT DE SACRIFICE" and a note written in French resembling a conversation at the bottom left. The drawing has a humorous and satirical tone.

artworks.title: L'Ame invisible; Mademoiselle Fifi
artworks.medium: 5-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a painting of theatrical posters for two plays, L'Âme Invisible and Mlle Fifi. The left side shows two figures in an intense moment with a poster for "L'Âme Invisible" below. The right side shows two figures at a table, with one in a yellow garment and holding a glass, and the other making a gesture. Various items like a bottle and a cigarette are present. The color palette is muted with spots of vibrant colors, showcasing elements in an illustrative style. This painting is in the style of Toulouse-Lautrec, known for depicting theatrical and Parisian life.

artworks.title: Venise sauvée (Venice Preserved)
artworks.medium: lithograph on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: The image is composed of undulating lines and shapes. Two human profiles are intertwined with the lines at the top. In the center, there are piercing eyes. The edges are framed with faces resembling theatrical masks.

artworks.title: Le Chariot de terre cuite
artworks.medium: lithograph in blue on pink wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring a theatrical program combined with an illustrative design. The left side contains text of a program for a performance titled "Le Chariot de Terre Cuite," detailing acts, participants, and roles. The right side features an illustration of a person standing behind a sculptural column with raised arms. Curvilinear organic shapes weave through the design, creating an ornate backdrop. The composition shows an Art Nouveau influence with flowing lines and integration of typography and illustration.

artworks.title: L'Argent
artworks.medium: 5-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: The image displays two individuals shown from the waist up, facing away from the viewer. The person on the left wears an oversized beige coat and short, light-colored hair styled upward. The individual on the right wears a dark coat and a tall black top hat with no visible facial features. The background is bold red. In the lower right, there is a table with a cloth that has text printed on it, titled "L'ARGENT." An elegant white outlined design frames the text, which includes names and roles related to a theatrical performance, with a small yellow flower-like detail on the tablecloth.
